pockets.name: Sevastopol bridgehead
pockets.note: The 17th Army fell back to Sevastopol after the Soviet offensive of 8 April (Simferopol 13 April); the city fell on 9 May 1944

Operation Bagration a week old: Polotsk, the Berezina at Borisov, Bobruisk taken (29 June), Slutsk; Army Group Centre broken; the line drawn after the remaining German units; the south as on 1 June

after Bagration and the Lvov–Sandomierz offensive: Narva, Tartu, the Soviet thrust to the Gulf of Riga at Tukums (31 July) cutting off Army Group North, Kaunas (taken 1 August), Suwalki, Bialystok, the Vistula at Warsaw-Praga, the Magnuszew and Baranow bridgeheads, Lvov (taken 27 July), Stanislav, and the unchanged Romanian front

1944-08-01.adjustments: Army Group North cut off by the Soviet thrust to Tukums (31 July – 20 August 1944) is not drawn as a pocket: the line runs to the coast west of Riga, and the Courland–Riga side is left on the German side.

sheets.note: after the Jassy–Kishinev operation and Romania’s change of sides (23 August): Narva and Tartu, the Baltic coast, East Prussia’s border, the Narew and the Vistula with the bridgeheads, the Carpathians, and in Romania the Carpathian passes (Romanian and Soviet forces against the German–Hungarian front in Transylvania) and the Danube to the Iron Gates

Tallinn (taken 22 September) and the Estonian mainland lost, the line before Riga, the Memel–Lithuanian front, the East Prussian border, the Narew and the Vistula (Warsaw rising), the Dukla pass and the Carpathians, Transylvania (Cluj and the Mures), and the Soviet advance into the Banat towards the Iron Gates

1944-10-01.adjustments: The line begins on the coast at the Latvian–Estonian border; the Moonsund islands (Saaremaa and Hiiumaa, German until October–November 1944) are kept on the German side by closing the Soviet side along the sea east of them.

sheets.note: Riga lost (13 October) and the Courland bridgehead, Memel encircled, the Gumbinnen–Goldap operation inside East Prussia, the Narew and the Vistula, the Carpathians and eastern Slovakia (Dukla), the Tisza from Chop to Szeged after the Debrecen battle, and Belgrade (taken 20 October): the map of 31 October (Akte 1224)

pockets.name: Saaremaa (Sworbe)
pockets.note: The Sworbe peninsula held until 24 November 1944

sheets.note: Courland and Memel, East Prussia, the Narew and the Vistula, the Carpathians, the Soviet advance between the Tisza and the Danube towards Budapest (the outskirts reached 4 November), and the Danube to Belgrade: the latest map before December in the series (13 November, Akte 1232)

1944-12-01.adjustments: The series breaks off with the map of 13 November 1944; the 1 December snapshot uses it, so the Soviet crossing of the Danube at Batina (late November) is not shown.
